clue.text: Gets around senior journalist's ways of working

indicators.note: to go around something is to surround it, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: to procure is to get or obtain
ED is short for editor, the senior journalist on a paper

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor has a habit of getting round the office rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets around' reads as dodging something, but 'around' is the container signal and 'Gets' supplies the outer word. ED is the standard crossword shorthand for an editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Procedures are established methods or routines followed when carrying out a task.

clue.text: Speed of some spaceships

indicators.note: 'some of' a word is only part of it, so the letters sit inside the next word

parts.note: sits in the letters after the opening S

explanation.surface: A question of how fast certain rockets travel.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is tucked inside sPACEships.
explanation.definitionFit: Pace is the rate of movement or progress, a straightforward synonym for velocity.

clue.text: Announced time for you and me

definitions.note: a phrase meaning belonging to us, matching the possessive pronoun

indicators.note: what is announced is spoken out, so the sound matters, not the spelling

parts.note: hours are units of time, and the H is silent when spoken

explanation.surface: Someone declares a moment set aside just for the two of us.
explanation.walkthrough: HOURS and OURS sound the same because the H in hours is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Ours is the possessive pronoun meaning belonging to us, the speaker plus the listener together.

clue.text: Reckoning mountaineer will flail about

indicators.note: to flail about is to thrash wildly, throwing letters into disorder

parts.note: taken as written, eleven letters

explanation.surface: A prediction that a climber is going to thrash around on the rock face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reckoning' reads as a forecast, but it is the definition in its counting sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Enumeration is the act of counting or listing items one by one, which is a form of calculation.

clue.text: Emerges and … decreases?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: comes out gradually, as a story or plan does
second meaning, read whimsically as de-creases: takes the creases out

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis and question mark flag a playful reading: 'decreases' is not getting smaller but removing creases, which is what you do when you open folded paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot or situation develops and becomes visible, and a folded sheet is opened out flat, losing its creases.

clue.text: Making plane when night approaches

definitions.meaning: first meaning: levelling a surface, as plane means flat

definitions.note: a phrase naming a time, standing for the noun
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the part of the day before dark

explanation.surface: A carpenter planes wood as darkness falls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plane' suggests an aircraft or the woodworking tool, but here it is the adjective for flat or level.
explanation.definitionFit: To even a surface is to smooth it flat, and the late part of the day leading into darkness has the same spelling.

clue.text: It brought back very loud disagreement

indicators.note: something brought back returns the way it came, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: taken as written
FF is fortissimo, the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: An old shouting match flares up again.
explanation.walkthrough: In music, F means loud (forte) and FF very loud (fortissimo).
explanation.definitionFit: A tiff is a petty quarrel, the kind of minor squabble between friends or partners.

clue.text: Regrettably intermixes as a last resort

indicators.note: something done regrettably has gone wrong, so the letters are put in a bad order

parts.note: taken as written, ten letters

explanation.surface: Someone sadly mixes things together only because nothing else is left.
explanation.walkthrough: IN EXTREMIS is Latin, literally 'in the furthest reaches', used in English for desperate circumstances.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase describes acting in an extreme emergency, when every other option has been exhausted.

clue.text: Flowery language suggesting waves

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ornate turns of phrase in speech or writing
second meaning: brandishes, as one does a sword or a hat

explanation.surface: Florid prose that hints at the sea's motion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waves' looks like a noun for the sea; it is the verb meaning brandishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornate decorative phrases are called by this name, and a person who brandishes something showily does the same as a verb.

clue.text: Character in La Belle et la Bête?

definitions.text: Character in La Belle et la Bête?

parts.words: Character in La Belle et la Bête?
parts.note: surface reading: a figure in the fairy tale, such as Belle or the Beast
setter's reading: a typographic mark printed in the title itself, the little hat over the E of Bête

explanation.surface: Asking who appears in the French fairy tale Beauty and the Beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' points to a role in the story; it means a printed symbol. Look at the title's spelling, not its plot.
explanation.definitionFit: This accent, shaped like a small roof, sits on the vowel of the French word for beast, so it is literally a mark in the title.

clue.text: Fabulous captain seeing portent heading west

indicators.note: in an across entry, going west means reading right to left, backwards

parts.note: an omen is a sign of things to come

explanation.surface: A legendary sea captain spots a bad sign as he sails west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fabulous' here means belonging to fable or fiction, not wonderful.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain Nemo commands the submarine Nautilus in Jules Verne's novel, a fictional figure from an adventure story.

clue.text: Elder recites awfully locally sourced food?

definitions.note: the question mark marks a definition by example: it is local only to Leicester

indicators.note: something done awfully is done badly, so the letters come out jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An older person reads out, badly, a list of local produce.
explanation.walkthrough: Red Leicester is a hard orange English cheese named after the county of Leicestershire, so it is 'locally sourced' only if you live there.
explanation.definitionFit: This cheese takes its name from the place where it is made, so it is food tied to one locality.

clue.text: Felt professional

definitions.meaning: first meaning: underwent or sensed, as with an emotion

explanation.walkthrough: 'Felt' could be the fabric, but here it is the past tense of feel.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a past-tense verb for having lived through something and an adjective for someone seasoned and skilled.

clue.text: Badly upset rogue state's inhabitants

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so the letters end up out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The citizens of a rogue nation are deeply distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rogue state' reads as a phrase, but 'rogue' belongs with 'upset' as fodder, and the definition is 'state's inhabitants'.
explanation.definitionFit: The people living in Portugal, a European country, are collectively called by this name.

clue.text: Cold weather curtailed small elves' dancing in type of clothing for summer

definitions.note: a noun phrase standing for the adjective describing such clothes

indicators.note: to curtail is to cut short, literally docking the tail, so the last letter goes

parts.note: sleet is cold wet weather, cut short by its final letter

indicators.note: letters that are dancing move about and change places

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
taken as written

explanation.surface: Little elves dance about in the sleet wearing light summer outfits.
explanation.walkthrough: SLEE(t) is followed by a jumble of S plus ELVES.
explanation.definitionFit: Garments without arms, such as vests and summer dresses, are described this way because they suit hot weather.

clue.text: Duck without much flesh in coating of rillettes in French city

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, shaped like O

indicators.note: one thing placed in another is enclosed by it
a coating is the outside layer, so only the outermost letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word
lean meat has little fat, a lean person little flesh

explanation.surface: A duck dish served with a thin layer of rillettes in a city in France.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a zero score in cricket, hence O. Rillettes is a French potted meat spread, which keeps the culinary scene going.
explanation.definitionFit: Orleans is a city on the Loire in central France, famous for Joan of Arc.

clue.text: Rodents: those who fetch and carry, we're told

indicators.note: what we are told reaches us by ear, so it is the sound that counts

parts.note: gofers are dogsbodies who 'go for' things

explanation.surface: Someone is informed that the office runners are a bunch of rats.
explanation.walkthrough: A gofer is an errand-runner, named because they 'go for' things.
explanation.definitionFit: Gophers are burrowing North American animals belonging to the rodent order, related to squirrels.

clue.text: Slightly edited thesis describing king's sculpture

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw round it, so one part goes around another
text that has been edited is rearranged a little, so the letters shift

parts.note: taken as written
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A dissertation about a monarch's statue has had a light edit.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the S and I of THESIS swap, hence 'slightly' edited; K then goes inside THE-ISS.
explanation.definitionFit: Rodin's famous marble of two embracing lovers carries this title, as does a Brancusi carving.

clue.text: Subversive spoon?

definitions.note: an adjective here, while the answer is a noun for such a person
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a troublemaker who stirs things up
second meaning: a utensil used to mix a drink or pot

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the spoon is only one example of a thing for mixing.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who deliberately provokes trouble is called this in British slang, and so is any implement that mixes liquids.

clue.text: Perhaps the army chaplain delivers this?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one of the armed forces, given by example
second meaning: a religious ceremony a minister leads

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a military padre leads a particular ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one sentence, but splits after 'army': each half is a separate meaning of the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: The army, navy and air force are each called an armed branch of this name, and a religious act of worship shares it.

clue.text: Plundering coarse cloth

definitions.meaning: first meaning: looting a captured town
second meaning: rough fabric such as hessian used for bags

explanation.surface: Looting rough fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: Both readings are standard, one a verb of pillage, the other a material.
explanation.definitionFit: To sack a city is to pillage it, and the rough woven fabric that sacks are made from is also called this.

clue.text: Atingle, seeing French birds

indicators.note: to be atingle is to be all aquiver, and quivering letters jump out of place

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher thrilled to spot some birds in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French birds' looks like the definition, but 'French' is fodder and 'birds' alone defines. 'Atingle' (tingling with excitement) is an unusual anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: These are olive-green songbirds of the finch family, common in European gardens.

clue.text: Sent up Arab leader's old poem

indicators.note: in a down entry, sending something up makes it read from bottom to top

parts.note: an emir is a ruler in the Arab world

explanation.surface: An Arab ruler's antique verse is mocked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sent up' suggests mockery; in a down clue it turns the word upside down. RIME is the archaic spelling of rhyme, as in Coleridge's Rime of the Ancient Mariner.
explanation.definitionFit: Rime is an archaic spelling for a rhyming verse, used in the title of Coleridge's famous ballad.

clue.text: Primarily inauspicious day, especially senatorially!

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the opening letters are wanted

parts.note: the initial letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: A day of ill omen, especially for Roman senators.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: Caesar was stabbed by senators on the Ides of March, so the day was unlucky above all for them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ides was a mid-month date in the Roman calendar, made notorious as the day of Julius Caesar's assassination in the Senate.

clue.text: Everyman's heading to find dingy venue where sinful behaviour occurred

indicators.note: the heading of something is its top, so the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the setter's name
a den is a small dingy room or lair

explanation.surface: The setter goes in search of a seedy dive where vice took place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dingy' stands for a dingy place, a den; the sin is the first one, Adam and Eve eating the forbidden fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The Garden of Eden is where the Bible places the first sin, when Adam and Eve disobeyed God.

clue.text: Start to battle cloud storage issue: that's an idea

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, which is all that is kept

parts.note: the opening letter
a cloud stores water that falls as rain
issue means offspring, as in 'died without issue'

explanation.surface: Someone begins to tackle a computer data-storage problem and has a bright thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cloud storage' suggests online data; it means what a cloud holds. 'Issue' in its legal sense means children.
explanation.definitionFit: A brainchild is an original plan or invention credited to one person, so it is a notion.

clue.text: Cinéaste describes this direction

indicators.note: to describe can mean to draw round, so the outer word encloses the letters

parts.note: the letters lie in the middle of the word, ignoring the accent

explanation.surface: A film-maker explains which way to go.
explanation.walkthrough: Accents are ignored, so ciNEASTe can be read without the acute mark: cin-EAST-e.
explanation.definitionFit: East is one of the four compass points, the bearing towards sunrise.

clue.text: Colonels' superiors tidied up debris surrounding Latvian capital

indicators.note: to surround is to enclose, so one part goes inside another
tidying rearranges things into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
Riga is the capital city of Latvia

explanation.surface: Senior officers clean up the rubble around Riga.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Latvian capital' could mean the letter L, but here it is the city.
explanation.definitionFit: In the British Army a brigadier ranks directly above a colonel, commanding a brigade.
